questions.question: A data scientist explains that their field sits within a broader discipline, and their latest project uses neural networks with dozens of layers. How do these three levels of technology relate to each other?

options.text: AI is the broadest discipline, ML is a subset of AI, and Deep Learning is a further specialization within ML
Deep Learning is the broadest category, with ML and AI as its specialized subsets
They are interchangeable terms that vendors use for the same set of algorithms
AI and ML are independent research fields that occasionally share techniques

questions.explanation: AI is the broadest field encompassing technologies that simulate human intelligence. Machine Learning is a subset focused on learning from data. Deep Learning is a specialized subset of ML using neural networks with multiple layers.

questions.question: An e-commerce platform wants to segment its customers into groups based on purchasing behavior, but no one has pre-labeled which group each customer belongs to. Which approach should the team use?

options.text: Reinforcement learning with a reward signal tied to purchase amounts
Clustering through unsupervised learning to discover natural groupings
Classification through supervised learning using historical sales labels
Semi-supervised learning combining a small set of group labels with the remaining data

questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning is ideal for finding patterns without predefined labels. Clustering algorithms group similar data points together, making it perfect for customer segmentation without prior categorization.

questions.question: A bank needs to approve or decline each credit card transaction within milliseconds to prevent fraud. Which inferencing strategy meets this requirement?

options.text: Scheduled batch jobs that process accumulated transactions every hour
Offline analysis of historical transactions to build risk profiles
Nightly ETL pipelines that flag suspicious activity for next-day review
Real-time inference that evaluates each transaction as it arrives

questions.explanation: Real-time inferencing processes data and returns predictions immediately, which is crucial for fraud detection where instant decisions are needed to approve or flag transactions as they occur.

questions.question: A game-playing agent starts with random moves, gradually improves by receiving points for winning and losing points for illegal moves. Which paradigm describes this learning process?

options.text: An agent optimizing its strategy through rewards and penalties from the environment
A model trained on a labeled dataset of winning and losing board positions
A clustering algorithm grouping similar game states without labels
A pretrained vision model fine-tuned on screenshots of the game board

questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning involves an agent learning through interaction with an environment and receiving feedback. The agent learns to maximize cumulative rewards over time through trial and error.

questions.question: A hospital stores patient records in a relational database with clearly defined columns for age, blood pressure, diagnosis code, and treatment outcome. What data category does this represent?

options.text: Semi-structured data stored in self-describing formats like JSON or XML
Unstructured data requiring specialized processing pipelines
Tabular data organized in structured rows and columns
Time-series data indexed sequentially by timestamp

questions.explanation: Tabular data is organized in rows and columns like spreadsheets or database tables. This structured format is common in business applications and works well with traditional ML algorithms.

questions.question: A model performs extremely well on its training dataset, achieving 99% accuracy, but drops to 60% accuracy when evaluated on new data it has never seen. What problem does this indicate?

options.text: The model architecture has too few parameters to learn the patterns
The model has memorized the training data including its noise and does not generalize
The evaluation dataset is corrupted and needs to be cleaned
The training process terminated too early before convergence

questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too well, including noise and random fluctuations. This results in poor generalization to new, unseen data.

questions.question: A linear regression model produces nearly identical error rates on both training and test data, but both rates are unacceptably high. What is the most likely issue?

options.text: The model has memorized the training examples and cannot generalize
The model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in the data
The test dataset contains label errors that inflate the error rate
The learning rate was set too high during the optimization process

questions.explanation: Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in the data. It performs poorly on both training and test data because it cannot represent the complexity of the relationship.

questions.question: A medical imaging team has ten thousand X-rays, each tagged by a radiologist as either 'normal' or 'abnormal.' What makes this dataset distinct from one that lacks those tags?

options.text: The tagged dataset is encrypted while the untagged one is stored in plain text
The tagged dataset is smaller because adding labels removes duplicate images
The tagged dataset comes from verified sources while the untagged one does not
The tagged dataset pairs each input with a known output, enabling supervised training

questions.explanation: Labeled data includes both input features and corresponding output labels used in supervised learning. Unlabeled data contains only inputs without corresponding labels.

questions.question: An autonomous vehicle collects terabytes of dashcam video, audio recordings from its microphone array, and free-text incident reports from test drivers. What category best describes these data types?

options.text: Structured data organized in relational database tables
Tabular data arranged in rows with well-defined column schemas
Time-series data indexed by sequential timestamps
Unstructured data that lacks a predefined format

questions.explanation: Unstructured data lacks a predefined format and includes text documents, images, audio files, and videos. It requires specialized processing techniques for AI applications.

questions.question: A robotics startup trains a warehouse picking arm by having it attempt thousands of grasps, receiving a positive signal when it successfully picks up an item and a negative signal when it drops one. Which learning approach is this?

options.text: Supervised classification using labeled images of objects
Unsupervised clustering of object shapes and sizes
Optimization through interaction with the environment and feedback signals
Transfer learning from a pretrained language model

questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning involves an agent learning through interaction with an environment, receiving rewards for beneficial actions and penalties for undesirable ones.

questions.question: A data engineer transforms raw website clickstream logs into derived columns such as 'average session duration,' 'pages per visit,' and 'time since last purchase.' What is this process called?

options.text: Model distillation, which compresses a large model into a smaller one
Data augmentation, which generates synthetic training examples
Hyperparameter tuning, which optimizes model training configuration
Feature engineering, which creates informative input variables from raw data

questions.explanation: Feature engineering uses domain knowledge to create new input features that better represent the underlying problem, potentially improving model performance and interpretability.

questions.question: A team is building a CI/CD pipeline that automatically retrains their recommendation model when new data arrives, runs validation tests, and promotes the model to production if metrics improve. What discipline does this describe?

options.text: MLOps, which applies DevOps practices to the machine learning lifecycle
Data cataloging, which inventories available datasets for discovery
Model distillation, which compresses large models for deployment
Feature store management, which versions engineered input variables

questions.explanation: MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) streamlines taking ML models to production and maintaining them. It includes CI/CD for models, monitoring, and governance practices.

questions.question: A logistics company needs to predict package volumes for the upcoming holiday season using three years of daily shipment counts. Which inference approach is most appropriate for this non-urgent, large-scale prediction?

options.text: On-device edge inference for each package as it is scanned
Real-time inference returning a prediction within milliseconds
Batch inference that processes the full historical dataset on a schedule
Streaming inference that continuously processes a live data feed

questions.explanation: Batch inferencing processes large volumes of data at once on a scheduled basis. It's ideal for non-time-sensitive applications like seasonal demand forecasts or bulk predictions.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following machine learning paradigms require labeled training examples to learn? (Select 2)

options.text: Semi-supervised learning that leverages a small amount of labeled data alongside unlabeled data
Supervised learning for classification and regression using input-output pairs
Reinforcement learning that relies on reward signals from the environment
Unsupervised learning for discovering clusters without predefined labels

questions.explanation: Supervised learning requires fully labeled data for training. Semi-supervised learning uses a combination of labeled and unlabeled data. Unsupervised learning uses no labels, and reinforcement learning uses reward signals.
